# Motivation

Transversal gates act independently on corresponding physical qubits in each code block, so a single physical fault cannot spread within a block. No quantum code admits a universal set consisting entirely of transversal logical gates [@eastin2009restrictions]. A useful alternative is to choose codes with a transversal non-Clifford gate and connect them to a Clifford fault-tolerant scheme through magic-state distillation or code switching.

Bravyi and Haah introduced triorthogonal matrices as a systematic source of CSS codes with transversal $T$ action, possibly followed by a known Clifford correction [@bravyi2012magic].

# Triorthogonal matrices

For binary vectors $f,g\in\mathbb F_2^n$, write

$$
|f\cdot g|=\sum_{j=1}^nf_jg_j,
$$

and similarly for triple componentwise products.

::: {#def-triorthogonal-matrix .callout-note icon="false"}
## Definition: triorthogonal matrix

A binary matrix $G$ with rows $g^1,\ldots,g^m$ is triorthogonal when, for every set of distinct row indices,

$$
|g^a\cdot g^b|=0\pmod2
$$

and

$$
|g^a\cdot g^b\cdot g^c|=0\pmod2.
$$

Partition its rows into the even-weight submatrix $G_0$ and odd-weight submatrix $G_1$.
:::

Assume the rows of $G$ are independent and $G_1$ has $k$ rows $f^1,\ldots,f^k$. Let

$$
\mathcal G_0=\operatorname{rowspan}G_0,
\qquad
\mathcal G=\operatorname{rowspan}G.
$$

# Associated CSS code

Define a CSS code with

$$
X\text{-stabilizer space }\mathcal G_0,
\qquad
Z\text{-stabilizer space }\mathcal G^\perp.
$$

Because $\mathcal G_0\subseteq\mathcal G$, the two stabilizer spaces are orthogonal. The $k$ odd rows provide logical Pauli representatives

$$
\overline X_a=X(f^a),
\qquad
\overline Z_a=Z(f^a).
$$

Pairwise triorthogonality gives

$$
f^a\cdot f^b=\delta_{ab}\pmod2,
$$

so each logical pair anticommutes while distinct logical operators commute.

::: {#thm-triorthogonal-code-dimension .callout-important icon="false"}
## Theorem: encoded dimension

If $G$ has independent rows and $G_1$ contains $k$ rows, then the CSS construction above encodes $k$ logical qubits.
:::

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Proof

There are $n$ physical qubits, $\operatorname{rank}G_0$ independent $X$ stabilizers, and

$$
\dim\mathcal G^\perp=n-\operatorname{rank}G
$$

independent $Z$ stabilizers. Hence

$$
k_Q=n-\operatorname{rank}G_0-(n-\operatorname{rank}G)
=\operatorname{rank}G-\operatorname{rank}G_0=k.
$$
:::

Normalized logical basis states may be written

$$
|x_1\cdots x_k\rangle_L
=\frac{1}{\sqrt{|\mathcal G_0|}}
\sum_{g\in\mathcal G_0}
\left|g+\sum_{a=1}^kx_af^a\right\rangle.
$$

# Why triorthogonality controls transversal phase

Let $\omega=e^{i\pi/4}$, so

$$
T^{\otimes n}|v\rangle=\omega^{|v|}|v\rangle.
$$

For binary vectors $g^a$ and coefficients $x_a$, inclusion--exclusion modulo eight gives

$$
\left|\bigoplus_ax_ag^a\right|
\equiv
\sum_ax_a|g^a|
-2\sum_{a<b}x_ax_b|g^a\cdot g^b|
+4\sum_{a<b<c}x_ax_bx_c|g^a\cdot g^b\cdot g^c|
\pmod8.
$$

Terms involving four or more distinct rows carry a factor divisible by eight. Pairwise and triple even-overlap conditions force the remaining cross terms to produce at most a diagonal Clifford phase. With additional divisibility conditions on row weights and overlaps, those Clifford corrections vanish.

::: {#thm-triorthogonal-transversal-t .callout-important icon="false"}
## Theorem: transversal $T$

The CSS code associated with a triorthogonal matrix is preserved by transversal $T$, up to a diagonal Clifford correction determined by the row weights and overlaps. On the logical subspace, the non-Clifford part is a product of logical $T$ or $T^\dagger$ gates, with the sign fixed by convention [@bravyi2012magic].
:::

Thus “triorthogonal” alone should not be paraphrased as “$T^{\otimes n}$ equals exactly $T_L^{\otimes k}$.” The correction and phase convention must be computed.

# The fifteen-qubit example

Index the fifteen coordinates by the nonzero points $u\in\mathbb F_2^4$. Define evaluation vectors

$$
[1]_u=1,
\qquad
[x_i]_u=u_i,
\qquad i=1,\ldots,4.
$$

Let $G_1$ contain the all-ones row $[1]$ and let $G_0$ contain $[x_1],\ldots,[x_4]$. Their weights and overlaps are

$$
|[1]|=15,
\quad
|[x_i]|=8,
\quad
|[x_ix_j]|=4,
\quad
|[x_ix_jx_k]|=2
$$

for distinct indices. Hence the five-row matrix is triorthogonal. Moreover,

$$
\mathcal G^\perp
=\operatorname{span}\{[x_i],[x_ix_j]:1\le i<j\le4\},
$$

which has dimension ten. The resulting code is the $[[15,1,3]]$ punctured Reed--Muller code.

The logical Pauli operators may both be represented by the all-ones vector. For an affine linear word

$$
v=z_0[1]+\sum_{i=1}^4z_i[x_i],
$$

the weight is a multiple of eight when $z_0=0$, and is congruent to seven modulo eight when $z_0=1$. Therefore

$$
T^{\otimes15}|+\rangle_L
=T_L^\dagger|+\rangle_L
$$

under this choice of $T=\operatorname{diag}(1,e^{i\pi/4})$. Reversing the physical phase convention exchanges $T$ and $T^\dagger$.

# Fifteen-to-one magic-state distillation

Prepare fifteen noisy $T$-type resource states, project onto the code space using the stabilizer checks, reject on a nontrivial syndrome, and decode the surviving logical qubit. Because the code has distance three, every weight-one or weight-two input error is detected; the leading accepted output error is cubic in the input error rate. The protocol is therefore called “15-to-1.”

The usefulness of this construction is operational: Clifford gates and Pauli measurements implement the checking circuit, while the transversal phase relation transfers the non-Clifford resource to the logical output [@bravyi2005universal; @bravyi2012magic]. Resource estimates must also include acceptance probability, Clifford-circuit faults, and the target logical error rate.

# Relation to code switching

Triorthogonal codes suggest a division of labor:

1. store and manipulate data in a code optimized for locality and Clifford operations;
2. switch or teleport into a code with the required transversal non-Clifford gate;
3. apply the transversal gate and return.

Magic-state distillation and code switching are not automatically equivalent, but both consume an auxiliary code structure to evade the absence of a universal transversal gate set. Establishing a concrete conversion requires a fault-tolerant interface, syndrome handling, and a bound on error propagation; triorthogonality supplies only the transversal-phase component.
